version.changelog:
- Major refactor: restructured the project to simplify the directory and scripts.
- Added new scripts: generate_report.py, schedule_push.py, auto_run.sh, auto_run_feishu.sh, config.example.json.
- Removed legacy and redundant files from previous "stock-report-pro" subdirectory.
- Updated README.md and documentation to reflect the new file structure and usage.
- Improved overall maintainability and clarity of the codebase.

llm.summary: The skill's code and instructions match its stated purpose (generate stock reports and optionally push to Feishu), but there are inconsistencies and missing declarations (notably reliance on the openclaw CLI and python runtime) that you should review before installing or running it.

dimensions.detail: Name/description align with included scripts: generate_report.py produces HTML/PNG reports from Sina Finance data and schedule_push/auto_run_feishu.sh attempt to push reports to Feishu via the 'openclaw' CLI. However, the registry metadata declares no required binaries while the code clearly requires python3 and (for pushing) the openclaw CLI.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and scripts limit behavior to fetching market data from Sina Finance, rendering charts, writing outputs to disk, and optionally invoking the openclaw CLI to send a media message to Feishu. There are no instructions to read unrelated system files or exfiltrate arbitrary data. One small scope issue: schedule_push contains a hardcoded placeholder recipient ID (ou_xxx...) which must be replaced by the user.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only with bundled code). Dependencies are standard Python packages; pyppeteer (if used) will auto-download Chromium on first run which is expected but heavy. No remote install URLs or obscure downloads in the repository.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables in metadata, yet pushing requires the 'openclaw' CLI to be configured with Feishu credentials and the user's environment to allow that command. The manifest omits declaring required binaries (python3, openclaw) and does not document any credential requirements for push functionality — this mismatch could lead to surprising behavior or accidental pushes if the openclaw CLI is configured.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request persistent/system-wide changes. It writes output files to disk (default /tmp) and assumes cron usage if configured by the user; nothing indicates modification of other skills or global agent config.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to do what it says (generate stock reports and optionally push them), but check a few things before installing or running:
- The repository does not declare required binaries, but you need python3 to run the scripts and the openclaw CLI if you want Feishu push. Ensure you trust and understand the openclaw CLI configuration (it holds credentials used for pushes).
- schedule_push/auto_run_feishu.sh call 'openclaw message send' — make sure you replace placeholder recipient IDs and confirm where messages will be delivered.
- pyppeteer may download Chromium on first run (large download); run in an environment where this is acceptable.
- The code fetches data from Sina Finance (including an HTTP endpoint for K-line data); if you need encrypted transport or offline use, review and adjust URLs.
- Consider running the skill in an isolated environment (container/VM) the first time to observe behavior and verify no unexpected network or system access occurs.
If these points are acceptable and you trust the openclaw CLI setup on your machine, the skill is coherent with its stated purpose; otherwise treat it cautiously.
